mainTopic: When a Jew leaves his wine alone with a נכרי, when do we worry that the נכרי touched it and made it forbidden as יין נסך?
overview: This daf continues the משנה about a Jew who leaves his wine alone with a נכרי. First, the גמרא explains when the נכרי is afraid of being caught: if the owner might show up by a twisting road, the wine stays permitted. If he said "go and I will come after you," the נכרי feels safe. Next, it explains why the משנה needed both the shop case and the wagon-or-ship case. Then רבי יוחנן teaches that the argument about how much time is needed applies only to a lime seal. The גמרא defends this from a ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, based on an unnamed משנה that measures the time by fully opening the barrel. The גמרא then asks why we still don't leave sealed wine with נכרים today, and answers that it is because of the small air hole, the שייכא. Finally, רבא begins a new case about wine at the table of a גויה זונה, and his reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner came back by a twisting road
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the earlier case: the Jew returned to the carriers by a winding, unexpected route.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a case where he came to them by a twisting road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this point. It explains why the wine in the first case of the משנה stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The carriers could not tell where the owner might suddenly appear from. Because of that, they were afraid to touch the wine, and we do not need to worry that they did. Their fear works the same as if he were watching them.

phrases.english: Where he came to them by a twisting road.
phrases.notes: Since they couldn't tell where he'd pop up from, the carriers were scared to touch the wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised just before this section of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case more narrowly (an unexpected return route)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner was far away, so the carriers had a chance to touch the wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were afraid he could show up at any moment, so the wine stays permitted.

steps.title: Then the later case should be the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if fear of a sudden return is enough, the later case should also be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the later case should also be the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. It asks why the same reason does not also permit the wine in the later case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the later case, the משנה forbids the wine. But if the owner could also come back by a surprising road there, the carriers should be just as scared. So the reason from step 1 seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה

phrases.english: If so, the later case too?
phrases.notes: He means: the later case should also be permitted, but the משנה forbids it there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If fear of a surprise return protects the wine, it should protect it in the later case too, yet the משנה forbids it there.

steps.title: "Go and I will come after you" lets them relax
steps.stepSummary: In the later case, the owner told them he would come behind them, so they felt safe and might touch the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he told them, "Go, and I will come after you," they felt sure of themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows how the later case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the later case, the owner told them exactly how he would come: behind them. They know they will see him coming, so they are not afraid of being surprised. That makes it possible they touched the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Go, and I will come after you
Their minds are at ease; they feel sure of themselves

steps.whatToRemember: What matters is whether the נכרי is afraid of being caught. If he expects a surprise, the wine is permitted. If he knows how the owner will come, he feels safe.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר לָהֶם ״לְכוּ וַאֲנִי בָּא אַחֲרֵיכֶם״,
phrases.english: Since he said to them, "Go, and I will come after you,"
their minds are at ease.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a factual difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve the same fear of a surprise return.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the later case he told them he would come from behind, so they feel safe and the wine is forbidden.

steps.title: Why we need both cases: the gentile-case alone could fool us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two cases from the משנה and begins explaining why both are needed. The case of the נכרי alone would not teach us about a wagon or ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: one who leaves a נכרי in his shop, and one who puts his wine in a wagon or a ship. Both are needed. If it had taught only the case of the נכרי, we would say the reason is that he thinks, "Maybe the owner will come and see me." But in a wagon or ship, we might say he can take his ship far away and do whatever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes two similar cases from the משנה and starts a צריכא, an explanation of why both are needed. This step gives the first half of that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases have the same rule, so one seems unnecessary. The גמרא shows that the נכרי case alone would not cover a ship, because a ship can sail far away where nobody can see. So the ship case had to be written separately.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is needed (both cases are necessary)

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases end with the same rule. The צריכא is not saying the rules are different. It is only showing that we could not have figured out one case from the other.

phrases.english: One who leaves a gentile in his shop, etc.

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּנִּיחַ יֵינוֹ בְּקָרוֹן אוֹ בִּסְפִינָה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One who places his wine in a wagon or on a ship, etc.
And it is necessary, for had it taught only the gentile case,
we would say it is because he thinks: perhaps he will come and see him;
but in a wagon or on a ship,
I would say that he takes his ship far off
and does whatever he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case of the נכרי alone would not teach the ship case, because a ship can sail out of sight.

steps.title: Why we need both cases: the ship case alone could fool us
steps.stepSummary: The ship case alone would not teach the shop case, because in a shop the נכרי can hold the door shut. So the משנה teaches us both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught only the wagon or ship, we would say the reason is that he thinks, "Maybe the owner will come by a different road, or stand on the riverbank, and see me." But a נכרי in a shop, we might say, can hold the door shut and do whatever he wants. So the משנה teaches us both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing the other side. Then it concludes that the משנה needed both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a ship, the נכרי is out in the open, so he might be seen from the shore or from another road. In a shop, he can close the door and feel completely hidden. Since each case has its own reason we might have said it is different, the משנה had to write both to show the rule is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is the same for the shop and for the wagon or ship. In each one, the נכרי is still afraid of being caught unless the Jew told him he was going far away.

phrases.english: And had it taught only the wagon or ship,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּסָבַר: דִּלְמָא אָתֵי בְּאוֹרְחָא אַחֲרִיתִי
phrases.english: we would say it is because he thinks: perhaps he will come by another road
or stand on the riverbank and see me;
but a gentile in his shop, I would say,

phrases.aramaic: אָחֵיד לֵהּ לְבָבָא וְעָבֵיד כֹּל דְּבָעֵי,
phrases.english: holds the door shut and does whatever he wants;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכא that began in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases are needed. The same rule applies to the shop and to the wagon or ship.

steps.title: The time argument applies only to lime seals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the משנה's argument about how much time is needed to the case of a lime seal. With a clay seal, everyone agrees the time needed is enough to open the barrel, reseal it, and let the seal dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The argument is only about a seal made of lime. But with a seal of clay, everyone agrees: it must be enough time to open the barrel, seal it again, and let the seal dry.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא makes a new statement. He explains exactly where the argument in the משנה applies, meaning the argument about how long the Jew was gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small hole in a סיד seal can be patched without anyone noticing, so the opinions disagree about how much time is enough. With טיט, any patch would show. So the נכרי would have to remove the whole seal, put on a new one, and wait for it to dry. Everyone agrees that this full amount of time is needed before the wine becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Seal it again, and let it dry

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the time needed depends on how easily the נכרי could tamper with the barrel without being caught.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
The argument is about a lime seal;
but with a clay seal, everyone agrees:
enough time to open, reseal, and let it dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the argument in the משנה about how much time is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies only to סיד. With טיט, everyone requires enough time to open the barrel, reseal it, and let the seal dry.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the seal can be seen from above and below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל tells the חכמים that a resealed spot can be seen both from above and from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to the חכמים, 'But isn't the sealed spot noticeable both from above and from below?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. This is the setup. The next step explains why the ברייתא is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues that a נכרי will not drill a hole and patch it, because the patch can be seen from both sides. That is why he only worries about fully opening the barrel. The key detail is the phrase 'from above and from below.'

keyTerms.meaning: Its sealing, meaning the patched spot

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to the Sages:
But isn't its sealing noticeable
phrases.notes: He means the spot where a hole was drilled and then patched, so the נכרי would be afraid to do it.

phrases.english: both from above and from below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן's statement in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the dispute is only about a lime seal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording 'from above and from below' seems to fit only a clay seal. The next step spells this out.

steps.title: The wording fits clay, not lime
steps.stepSummary: If the dispute were about clay, the ברייתא makes sense. But a lime patch can only be seen from below, not from above.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say the dispute is about clay. That is why it says 'noticeable from above and from below.' But if you say the dispute is about lime: fine, it can be seen from below, but from above it cannot be seen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why the ברייתא is a problem for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clay patch shows on both sides. A lime patch blends in on top and shows only underneath. Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said 'both from above and from below,' he seems to be talking about clay. That goes against רבי יוחנן, who said everyone agrees about clay.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that the dispute is about a clay seal,
that is why it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: סִתּוּמוֹ נִיכָּר בֵּין מִלְּמַעְלָה וּבֵין מִלְּמַטָּה,
phrases.english: its sealing is noticeable both from above and from below.
But if you say
that the dispute is about a lime seal,
granted, it is noticeable from below,
but from above it is not noticeable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּשֶׁל טִיט מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the problem raised by the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the dispute is only about a lime seal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'From above and from below' only fits clay. So the dispute seems to be about clay, against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answered both possibilities
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not know which seal the חכמים meant. So he said: with clay it shows on both sides, and with lime it at least shows from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was רבן שמעון בן גמליאל who did not know what the חכמים meant. This is what he told them: 'If you mean clay, the sealing shows from above and from below. If you mean lime, fine, it doesn't show from above, but at least it shows from below.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was covering both kinds of seals, because he was unsure which one the חכמים meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From above and from below' was his answer only for clay. For lime he admitted it shows only from below, and that was still enough for him. So the ברייתא does fit רבי יוחנן's view that the real dispute is about lime.

phrases.english: It was Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
who did not know what the Rabbis were saying,
and this is what he said to them:
If you are speaking of clay,

phrases.aramaic: סִתּוּמוֹ נִיכָּר בֵּין מִלְּמַעְלָה וּבֵין מִלְּמַטָּה,
phrases.english: its sealing is noticeable both from above and from below;
and if you are speaking of lime,
granted that from above it is not noticeable,
from below, at any rate, it is noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הוּא דְּלָא יָדַע מַאי קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 7 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא as a two-part answer covering both cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'from above and from below' showed the dispute was about clay.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answered for both cases. For lime, he relied on the patch showing from below.

steps.title: How the חכמים answer back
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the נכרי is not worried, because the owner won't think to flip the seal over. Also, sometimes the lime hardens and the patch doesn't show at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? Since it can't be seen from above, the נכרי doesn't think the owner will turn it over and look. Or another answer: sometimes the lime hardens well, and nothing shows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חכמים are not convinced by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'it shows from below' argument about lime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two answers. First, the נכרי only fears what the owner will check, and nobody turns the seal over to look underneath. Second, sometimes the lime seals so firmly that even from below the patch can't be seen. Either way, the חכמים still worry that he drilled and patched it.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
since from above it is not noticeable,
it does not enter his mind
that the owner will turn it over and see it.
Alternatively, sometimes it seals firmly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' reply to the argument of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defending the חכמים' position with two separate reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a lime patch shows from below, maybe the חכמים have no reason to worry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נכרי doesn't expect anyone to look underneath, or the patch may not show at all.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because an unnamed משנה follows his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, since we learned an unnamed משנה that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final practical ruling in this dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה is taught without a name, it usually shows the accepted view. Since such a משנה agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבא rules like him. In practice, we only worry if there was enough time to open, reseal, and dry the seal, not just to drill and patch.

keyTerms.meaning: Unnamed, a ruling taught without saying who said it

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about a lime seal (רבי יוחנן). The חכמים worry the נכרי drilled and patched it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the patch would show from below, so he only worries about a full opening. The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for how long a נכרי must be alone with sealed wine before we worry about it.

phrases.english: Rava says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
since we learned an unattributed mishna in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dispute with a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because an unnamed משנה agrees with him.

steps.title: The unnamed משנה that follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the unnamed משנה that agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: sealed barrels are permitted unless there was enough time to open, reseal, and let the new seal dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a Jew was eating with a נכרי and left jugs of wine on the table and a jug on the side table, then went out. What is on the table is forbidden, and what is on the side table is permitted. If he told the נכרי, 'Mix and drink,' even the side-table wine is forbidden. Open barrels are forbidden, and sealed ones are permitted, unless there was enough time to open, reseal, and let the seal dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which unnamed משנה רבא relied on when he ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last line of the משנה measures the time by how long it takes to open the barrel, meaning remove the whole seal, then reseal it and let it dry. It does not measure by drilling a small hole and patching it. That matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds that a drilled patch would be noticed, so the only worry is a full opening. Since this line has no name on it, it counts as an unnamed משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A side table, away from where people eat
Mix and drink (permission to touch the wine)
And reseal, and the new seal dries

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הָיָה אוֹכֵל עַל הַשּׁוּלְחָן עִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: As we learned: if he was eating at the table with him,
phrases.notes: A Jew is eating with a נכרי.

phrases.english: and left jugs on the table,
and a jug on the side table, and left them and went out —
what is on the table is forbidden,
what is on the side table is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: הֱוֵי מוֹזֵג וְשׁוֹתֶה —
phrases.english: and if he said to him: Mix and drink —
phrases.notes: "Mix" means mixing water into the wine, the way wine was drunk then.

phrases.english: even what is on the side table is forbidden.
Open barrels are forbidden, sealed ones are permitted,
unless there was time to open, reseal, and let it dry.
phrases.notes: This is the key line. It says 'open', meaning take off the whole seal, not just drill a small hole and patch it. That fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the unnamed משנה that רבא relied on in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The unnamed last clause of the משנה: 'enough time to open, reseal, and dry'

steps.title: Isn't רבא's ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since an unnamed משנה already rules this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: if the משנה already rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, why did he bother to say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה. So רבא seems to be telling us something we already know. The next step explains what he added.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבא's ruling was needed, given the משנה in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unnamed משנה already sets the הלכה, so רבא's ruling adds nothing.

steps.title: One might have thought the whole clause was רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that the last clause is a true unnamed משנה, not a continuation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches the whole clause. So רבא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבא is telling us that the line about sealed barrels is unnamed, not part of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the line were still רבן שמעון בן גמליאל speaking, it would just be one opinion against the חכמים. Then the rule of following an unnamed משנה would not apply. רבא teaches that it is a separate unnamed line, so the הלכה follows it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's חידוש is not the rule itself but that the sealed-barrel line is an unnamed משנה, so the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָתָנֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches the whole clause?
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling has a new point: who the author of the clause is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sealed-barrel line is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own words, so it is not an unnamed משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is an unnamed משנה, so the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Then why don't we leave wine with a נכרי today?
steps.stepSummary: If we are not worried about resealing or forged seals, why do we still not leave sealed wine with a נכרי nowadays?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we hold like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who is not worried about an opened hole, and the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר, who is not worried about forgery, why nowadays don't we leave wine with נכרים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about common practice: the rulings seem to allow sealed wine with a נכרי, yet people don't do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two lenient rulings are put together. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a resealed hole shows, and רבי אליעזר says we don't worry that a seal was forged. With both of those, sealed wine should be safe, so the practice needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole opened in the barrel (and resealed)

phrases.english: And since we hold
like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
who is not worried about an opened hole,
and the halakha is like Rabbi Eliezer
who is not worried about forgery,
phrases.notes: This is a different earlier discussion: whether a נכרי might fake a seal.

phrases.english: nowadays, what is the reason
that we don't leave wine in the hands of gentiles?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ruling in step 11 and asks about current practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the practice of not leaving sealed wine with נכרים, despite the lenient rulings.

steps.title: Because of the barrel's small air hole
steps.stepSummary: The reason is the שייכא, the small hole in the barrel that the נכרי could use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the worry today is a different one, the small air hole in the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Resealing and forgery are not the problem. Barrels have a tiny hole for smelling the wine, and a נכרי could widen it a little and get to the wine. That is why we still don't leave wine with them.

keyTerms.meaning: A small air hole in a barrel for smelling the wine

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the lenient views, yet wine is not left with a נכרי because of the שייכא.

phrases.english: Because of the air hole.
phrases.notes: A tiny hole used to smell the wine; a נכרי might widen it a bit and drink from it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is the שייכא, which a נכרי could widen to get at the wine.

steps.title: Wine at the table of a non-Jewish prostitute is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that when Jews dine at the table of a גויה זונה, the wine is permitted, and begins to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a non-Jewish prostitute, with Jews dining at her table, the wine is permitted. Granted, the desire for sin overpowers them,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new case and gives a lenient ruling. His sentence continues on the next amud, where he finishes his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the Jews are too distracted to watch the wine, so the woman could touch it. רבא admits they are overcome by desire, but the explanation of why the wine is still permitted comes next.

phrases.english: Rava said:
a non-Jewish prostitute, and Jews are dining at her place —
the wine is permitted,
granted that the desire for sin overpowers them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, not connected to the barrel discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine at a table where Jews dine with a גויה זונה is permitted, even though they are distracted by desire (reasoning continues).
